where: Section 1, table instructions vs the figure
problem: The text tells the student to make a table with five columns — E, N, next N, previous N, and the product — but the figure shows only three columns (E, N, product). A student copying the figure cannot see which next and previous northings produced each product, which is the one thing the table is meant to make visible.
fix: Either show all five columns in the figure (E, N, N_next, N_prev, E × (N_next − N_prev)), or change the text to say: one row per corner with columns E, N and the product E × (next N − previous N), reading the next and previous northings from the rows above and below.

problem: At corner A the substitution is written as 0 × (30 − 0), but the rule is E × (N_next − N_prev) and at A the next northing is N_B = 0 and the previous is N_C = 30, so the bracket must be (0 − 30). The value is still 0, so the area is right, but the shown order of subtraction is reversed and a student will copy it.

DMD is called 'the older name for the same job', but double meridian distance is a quantity used inside the DMD method, not a name for a method, and it is never defined. The double-area relation is also stated before the reader knows what DMD means.
fix: Write: the double-meridian-distance (DMD) method is the older route to the same double area, worked from latitudes (northing changes) and departures (easting changes). The meridian distance of a line is measured from a reference meridian to the midpoint of the line; its double is the DMD, and double area = Σ (DMD × latitude) over all lines, with signs.

problem: 'Multiply each easting by the change in northing' can be read as the northing change along the line, N_next − N_i, whereas the formula uses N_next − N_prev, the difference between the corners on either side of the corner being processed.
fix: Say: multiply each easting by the difference between the northings of the corners on either side of it (next minus previous), and add.
